newsletter.subject: Calloway housing bill clears the Senate
newsletter.text:
THE BIG ONE

The Calloway state Senate passed the Starter Homes Act by a vote of 31 to 18 on Friday. The bill lets developers build up to four homes on lots currently zoned for one, near transit stops, and sets a goal of 12,000 new homes a year.

Governor Ines Halvorsen has said she will sign it, and her office expects to do so by December 5.

Supporters, including the Calloway Builders Council, say the bill will bring down rents over time. Opponents, led by Senator Wade Prentice, argue that it overrides local control and that suburbs will see more traffic without new roads.

The bill also creates a $250 million fund for water and sewer upgrades in towns that add housing. Cities have until July 1 to update their zoning codes.

ALSO TODAY
- A bill to cap ticket resale prices stalled in committee.
- The state's rainy-day fund hit a record $3.9 billion.
